title: Model bundle manifest 1
description: The `manifest.json` at the root of an ImageProcessor model bundle. A bundle is an immutable, content-addressed tarball whose digest is the SHA-256 of the tarball itself; `manifest.sig` is the Ed25519 detached signature over the exact bytes of this document. The manifest is the only thing a bundle may say about itself, and it is verified, never trusted: the component checks the tarball digest, then the signature when the profile requires one, then extracts under path, count, size, and ratio limits, then checks every per-file digest against `files`, then this schema, and only then decides whether the declared task family and providers are supported. No bundle-supplied code is ever executed.

schemaVersion.description: The manifest contract version. The component refuses a bundle whose version it does not implement rather than guessing at the shape.

modelId.description: The model's published id. A route's `modelRef.id` matches it.

version.description: The model's published version. Identity on the wire is the tarball digest, so a version is a label for people, not the thing the component pins to.

files.title: Per-file digests
files.description: Every file the bundle carries, keyed by its path relative to the bundle root, with its SHA-256 as the value. Extraction checks each one; a file that is present but unlisted, or listed but absent, fails staging.

minOnnxRuntime.description: The lowest ONNX Runtime version that can load this model. A device running an older runtime refuses the bundle instead of failing on the first inference.

providersPermitted.description: The execution providers this model may run on, in preference order. Staging refuses the bundle when none of them appears in the device's `runtime.providers`.

providerPolicy.description: How strictly `providersPermitted` binds. `requireListed`: the session must be assigned one of the listed providers, and a route whose device cannot supply one is blocked rather than run elsewhere. `preferListed`: the listed providers are tried in order and `CPUExecutionProvider` may serve as a fallback, which the device honors only when `runtime.allowCpuOnly` is set.

inputs.description: The model's input tensors, as the graph declares them.

outputs.description: The model's output tensors, as the graph declares them. The task family interprets them, so an output set no family can read is refused at staging.

dynamicBatch.description: Whether the input shapes carry a dynamic batch axis. The scheduler micro-batches only when this is `true`, so a static-batch model is never handed more than one image at a time.

family.description: The built-in task family that turns the raw outputs into the normalized result the decision rules evaluate.

familyParams.description: The parameters the declared family needs. Its shape depends on `family`; see the per-family conditions at the end of this schema.

maxResultItems.description: How many items the normalized output may carry: classes, detections, or segment classes. It bounds both the published message and the evidence sidecar.

estimatedDeviceMiB.description: The publisher's estimate of the device memory one resident session needs. GPU admission starts from this number and refines it with measurements once the model has run.

measuredDeviceMiB.title: Measured memory profiles
measuredDeviceMiB.description: Measured profiles per GPU class, which supersede `estimatedDeviceMiB` on a matching device.

loadPeakMiB.description: The transient peak observed while the session loads.

steadyMiB.description: The steady-state footprint of the resident session.

warmup.description: The golden samples a session runs before it serves any job. A model that cannot reproduce its own goldens on the target provider degrades its routes instead of answering.

compatibilityKeys.title: Engine cache compatibility keys
compatibilityKeys.description: The dimensions a cached execution-provider engine is keyed by, as a flat map of names to values. A cached engine is reused only when every key matches the current device, driver, and runtime. Well-known keys are `precision`, `shapeProfile`, `gpuClass`, `cudaVersion`, `tensorrtVersion`, and `onnxruntimeVersion`.

keyId.description: The signing key that produced `manifest.sig`, named as it appears in the device's `signing.trustedKeys`. It is `null` on an unsigned bundle, which a device with `signing.required` refuses.

transformVersion.description: The version of the decode and preprocessing contract this bundle expects. It is recorded on every job and every result, so a preprocessing change shows up as a different transform version rather than as a silent shift in the numbers.

name.description: The tensor's name in the graph.

shape.description: The tensor's shape. A positive integer is a fixed axis; a string names a dynamic axis, and the name `N` is reserved for the batch axis the scheduler batches along.

preprocess.title: Decode and preprocessing
preprocess.description: How an executor cell turns decoded pixels into the model's input tensor. The component applies exactly this and nothing else, so two bundles that share a transform version and a preprocess block produce comparable numbers. The pipeline is: decode, reduce a high-bit-depth image per `highBitDepthMode`, swap to `colorOrder`, resize per `resize`, apply `(pixel * scale - mean) / std`, then lay the result out as `layout` in `dtype`.

inputName.description: The input tensor the preprocessed image binds to. Omit it on a single-input model.

batchAxis.description: Whether the input tensor carries a leading batch axis. Omit it to infer the axis from the input's declared rank.

mode.description: How the source image reaches the model's input size. `letterbox`: scale to fit, then pad with `padColor`, which preserves aspect ratio and is what box coordinates are un-letterboxed from. `stretch`: scale both axes independently. `centerCrop`: scale the short side, then crop the center. `none`: feed the image as decoded, which needs a fully dynamic input shape.

width.description: The model input width in pixels. Every mode but `none` needs it.

height.description: The model input height in pixels. Every mode but `none` needs it.

interpolation.description: The resampling filter. It is part of the numeric contract, so changing it changes the transform version.

padColor.description: The fill for `letterbox` padding, as one value for every channel or one value per channel. It is expressed in `colorOrder` and in the source pixel scale, before normalization.

padMode.description: Where the scaled image sits inside the padded canvas. `center` splits the padding evenly; `topLeft` puts all of it on the right and bottom.

scale.description: The factor applied to each raw pixel value before mean subtraction. Use `0.00392156862745098` to map `0..255` onto `0..1`.

mean.description: The mean subtracted after scaling, as one value for every channel or one value per channel, in channel order.

std.description: The standard deviation divided out after mean subtraction, as one value for every channel or one value per channel. No entry may be zero.

layout.description: The axis order of the input tensor.

colorOrder.description: The channel order the model expects. Decoded images are RGB, so `BGR` reverses them before anything else reads a channel.

dtype.description: The element type of the input tensor. A `uint8` model takes raw samples, so it may not also declare a `scale`, `mean`, or `std`.

highBitDepthMode.description: What happens to a 16-bit image. `scaleTo8Bit` reduces it to the 0..255 range the manifest's constants are written in, so an 8-bit manifest serves a 16-bit image. `raw` keeps the full range.

decisionRules.title: Decision rules
decisionRules.description: The rules that turn one normalized output into the result's `decision`. Paths are JSONPath over the normalized output, so a rule can name any field its family produces. A rule that cannot be evaluated - a path that matches nothing, a confidence that is not a number, an `outcomeOnFail` of `CLEAR` - holds the image rather than clearing it.

pass.description: The expression that decides the outcome.

confidence.description: The number reported as `decision.confidence`, either a literal or a JSONPath that resolves to one. Omit it when the family produces no single confidence.

threshold.description: The number reported as `decision.threshold`, either a literal or a JSONPath that resolves to one, so a consumer can see the bar that was applied.

outcomeOnPass.description: The outcome when the expression holds. An advisory model sets it to `HOLD` so a pass still requires a human.

outcomeOnFail.description: The outcome when the expression does not hold. `FAIL` classes the failure as a defect rather than a doubt. `CLEAR` is not available here.

failOnEmpty.description: Whether a path that matches nothing is a plain failure rather than a broken rule. It is what lets a rule such as 'there are no defects' evaluate on an image with no detections at all.

decisionExpression.title: Decision expression
decisionExpression.description: A leaf comparison, or a group of expressions. Groups nest to any depth.

oneOf.title: Any of
oneOf.description: Holds when at least one child holds.

decisionLeaf.title: Leaf comparison
decisionLeaf.description: One comparison against one JSONPath. A path that matches several values is a claim about every match: `$.detections[*].label != washer` means no detection is a washer.

path.description: A JSONPath over the normalized output, starting at the document root `$`.

op.description: The comparison. `>=`, `>`, `<=`, and `<` need numbers on both sides. `==` and `!=` compare against the literal in `value` and work for numbers, strings, and booleans. `exists` and `absent` describe the match set and take no `value`. `count>=` compares the size of the match set against `value`.

value.description: The literal the path is compared against. `exists` and `absent` take none.

channelValue.title: Per-channel constant
channelValue.description: One value applied to every channel, or one value per channel in channel order.

input.description: The raw input tensor, as little-endian binary matching `dtype` and `shape`.

inputName.description: The input tensor the sample binds to. Omit it on a single-input model.

dtype.description: The element type of the sample's binary input.

shape.description: The fully resolved shape of the sample's binary input. A warmup sample has no dynamic axes.

tolerances.title: Warmup tolerances
tolerances.description: How far a warmup run may drift from its golden before the bundle is refused. Every provider produces slightly different floating-point results, so a tolerance of zero would refuse every GPU.

absolute.description: The largest permitted absolute difference per element.

relative.description: The largest permitted relative difference per element.

boxIou.description: The smallest permitted intersection over union between a golden box and its match, used when `compare` is `normalized` on a detection model.

provenance.title: Provenance
provenance.description: Who published the bundle and what it came from. It is carried into the evidence sidecar, so a result can be traced back to a training run.

publishedAt.description: When the bundle was published, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

sourceModel.description: The upstream model the bundle was exported from.

trainingRun.description: The training run or experiment identifier.

datasetVersion.description: The dataset the model was trained on.

license.description: The license the model is distributed under.

gitRevision.description: The revision of the pipeline that produced the bundle.

labelSet.title: Class labels
labelSet.description: The class names, in model index order. A family with neither `labels` nor `numClasses` cannot name what it found.

numClasses.description: How many classes the head predicts, when the bundle names a count rather than labels. The normalized output then reports `class-<index>`.

activation.description: The activation applied to the raw scores. `softmax` makes the class set sum to one, `sigmoid` scores each class independently, and `none` reports the raw value.

topK.description: How many classes the normalized output keeps, after sorting by descending score. `maxResultItems` bounds it further.

scoreThreshold.description: The lowest score a class needs to appear in the output.

outputName.description: The output tensor holding the scores. Omit it on a single-output model.

detectionParams.title: Detection parameters
detectionParams.description: `decode` selects how the head is read. `yoloxGrid` reads an anchor-free grid and needs `strides`; `decodedBoxes` reads a head that already emits boxes, scores, and classes.

decode.description: How the raw outputs become boxes.

scoreThreshold.description: The lowest score a detection needs to survive filtering.

iouThreshold.description: The intersection over union above which suppression drops the weaker box of the same class.

maxDetections.description: How many detections survive suppression. It defaults to `maxResultItems`.

strides.description: The feature-map strides of the grid, smallest first. `yoloxGrid` requires it.

objectness.description: Whether the grid head emits an objectness column before the class scores. The reported score is objectness times class score.

scoreActivation.description: The activation applied to the class scores.

objectnessActivation.description: The activation applied to the objectness column.

outputName.description: The output tensor holding the grid. Omit it on a single-output model.

outputNames.title: Output roles
outputNames.description: Which output tensor plays which role on a `decodedBoxes` head.

count.description: A tensor naming how many of the fixed-size rows are real.

scoresLayout.description: Whether the score tensor carries one score per box, or a full class vector per box.

boxFormat.description: How the decoded box coordinates are laid out.

boxCoordinates.description: Whether decoded coordinates are already in `[0, 1]`. `pixels` divides them by the model input size before un-letterboxing.

classIndexOffset.description: Subtracted from every class index the head reports, for a head that reserves index zero for background.

applyNms.description: Whether to suppress overlapping boxes. Set it to `false` for a head that already suppressed them.

segmentationParams.title: Segmentation parameters
segmentationParams.description: `argmax` gives every label an entry, including the ones with no pixels, so a rule such as 'no defect pixels' evaluates on a clean image. `threshold` reports the single class named by `positiveLabel`.

mode.description: How the class map is read. `argmax` takes the highest-scoring class per pixel; `threshold` takes every pixel over `threshold` for one class.

outputLayout.description: The axis order of the output class map.

activation.description: The activation applied across the class axis before the map is read.

threshold.description: The per-pixel score at which a pixel joins the class, in `threshold` mode.

positiveLabel.description: The label the `threshold` mode reports. It defaults to the last label.

minPixels.description: The smallest region reported, in class-map pixels. It suppresses single-pixel speckle.

ignoreIndex.description: A class index excluded from the summary, usually the background.

outputName.description: The output tensor holding the class map. Omit it on a single-output model.

anomalyParams.title: Anomaly parameters
anomalyParams.description: An anomaly head scores the whole image, so it names no classes.

source.description: Where the image-level score comes from. `scalar`: the head emits it directly. `mapMax` and `mapMean`: reduce the per-pixel anomaly map, which also produces the heatmap summary.

threshold.description: The score at which the image counts as anomalous, in the same units as the reported score. It is republished on every result.

activation.description: The activation applied to the raw score.

direction.description: Which end of the range is anomalous. A similarity head sets `lowerIsAnomalous`.

normalization.title: Score normalization
normalization.description: Maps the raw score onto `[0, 1]` so a threshold reads the same across models.

min.description: The raw score that maps to `0`.

max.description: The raw score that maps to `1`.

outputName.description: The output tensor holding the score or the map. Omit it on a single-output model.

executionProvider.title: ONNX Runtime execution provider
executionProvider.description: An execution provider name as ONNX Runtime reports it.

bundlePath.description: A path relative to the bundle root, with `/` separators. It is never absolute and never traverses upward; extraction rejects anything else before this schema is even reached.

hex256.description: A SHA-256 digest as 64 lowercase hex characters, without a prefix.
